page: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an ARM-based virtual server powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs using the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the a1.2xlarge is positioned in the lower-to-middle tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield average results, with scores of 1491.99 and 11904.08 respectively. However, memory bandwidth performance is weak to poor, with large block read bandwidth at 23.51 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 8.88 GB/sec. Computational benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (410.0) and multi-core (2143.0) reflect a lower-tier performance profile, alongside weak results in software compilation (3648.0) and database operations (2462.51).

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the a1.2xlarge offers a budget-friendly entry point into ARM64 development and testing. The absence of hyperthreading (1.0 thread per core) ensures dedicated physical core execution, though the lack of advanced vector extensions (AVX) and matrix extensions limits its utility for intensive mathematical or machine learning workloads. It is best suited for lightweight containerized applications, basic web serving, and ARM64 software compilation pipelines that do not require high memory bandwidth or local storage.
